findings.title: Webhook duplicate-delivery example is vacuous w.r.t. the uniqueness invariant (5-minute dedupe masks guard+index deletion)
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §9.1 duplicate delivery -> exactly one row; rule 26 falsifiability; §3 invariant is the production mechanism for redeliveries >5 min apart
findings.evidence: spec/jobs/stripe_webhook_handler_subscription_events_spec.rb:~111 — both deliveries run inside the interactor's 5-minute dedupe window with byte-identical event_params; with conversion_duplicate_exists? and the partial index both deleted, the dedupe still blocks row 2 and every assertion passes.
findings.recommendation: Backdate the first row's created_at past 5 minutes (update_column) or travel between deliveries so the uniqueness invariant is the enforcing mechanism.

findings.title: Ledger-failure isolation example cannot distinguish the insertion's own rescue from the branch's outer swallow tier, and its raising stub is never asserted
findings.spec_requirement: SPEC §5.2 (own begin/rescue, never reaches existing tiers) + §9.1 (a ledger failure does not break them); rule 26
findings.evidence: stripe_webhook_handler_subscription_events_spec.rb ledger-failure example — not_to raise_error is satisfied by the pre-existing outer rescue StandardError tier (stripe_webhook_handler_job.rb ~336-346) even if the insertion's own rescue is deleted; the three existing-behavior assertions precede the insertion point so they pass regardless; deleting the ENTIRE insertion also passes because the raising CreateSubscriptionEvent stub has no have_received(:call) assertion.
findings.recommendation: Add expect(CreateSubscriptionEvent).to have_received(:call) plus a Rails.logger spy asserting the insertion's ledger-specific error message (proving the own rescue handled it, not the outer tier).
